'''Ora Kedem''' ({{Langx|he|אורה קדם}}; 2 July 1924 – 23 February 2026) was an Austrian-born Israeli chemist who was a professor at the [[Weizmann Institute of Science]] and [[Ben-Gurion University of the Negev]], and a recipient of the 1961 [[Israel Prize]] for [[life sciences]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://wis-wander.weizmann.ac.il/people-made-institute/life-science|title=A Life in Science - News, Features and Discoveries from the Weizmann Institute of Science|date=26 November 2013|work=Weizmann Wonder Wander|access-date=2 April 2018|language=en}}</ref>

==Biography==
Josefa Katz (later Ora Kedem) was born in Vienna. Her mother was a seamstress and her father ran a perfume business. After the [[Anschluss]], when Austria was annexed by the Nazis in 1938, the family  businesses were closed down.  Her brother and sister had already immigrated to Palestine with the [[Youth Aliya]] movement and her father immigrated in the framework of [[Aliya Bet]]. Kedem and her mother remained in Austria until 1940. Kedem, then 16 years old, boarded a ship on the Danube en route to Palestine.<ref>[https://www.weizmann.ac.il/president/spotlight-stories/memoriam-prof-ora-kedem-1924-2026-whose-discoveries-contributed-ascent-water In memoriam: Prof. Ora Kedem 1924-2026]</ref>

==Scientific career==
In 2005, she was elected a member of the [[National Academy of Engineering]] for contributions to the [[thermodynamics]] of irreversible transport processes and the development of separation processes for the treatment of water and wastewater.

Kedem died on 23 February 2026, at the age of 101.<ref>{{Cite web |last=moked2 |date=24 February 2026 |title=אורה קדם ז"ל |url=https://yediot-evel.co.il/%D7%90%D7%95%D7%A8%D7%94-%D7%A7%D7%93%D7%9D-%D7%96%D7%9C/ |access-date=25 February 2026 |website=ידיעות אחרונות מודעות אבל {{!}} קו ישיר 077-9967000 ☎️ |language=he-IL}}</ref>
